definition: Server-Side Rendering is a core concept in React Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Server-Side Rendering is
theory.body: Server-Side Rendering describes the methods and patterns used within React Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Server-Side Rendering is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Server-Side Rendering matters
theory.body: Without Server-Side Rendering, systems built with React Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Server-Side Rendering works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Server-Side Rendering follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Server-Side Rendering.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Server-Side Rendering
theory.body: Server-Side Rendering offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
